_note: Provider facts as DATA (names, API hosts, the owner's setup steps). The Python code stays provider-neutral; nothing here is logic.

google_search_console.name: Google Search Console
steps: In Google Cloud Console: create (or pick) a project and enable the 'Google Search Console API'.
Create a service account in that project and a JSON key for it; save the file as {folder}\gsc_service_account.json (nobody else needs to see it).

In Search Console, open this client's property -> Settings -> Users and permissions -> Add user: add the service account's e-mail ({identity}) with at least Restricted permission. (If the property belongs to the client, ask them to add that e-mail.)
Alternative without a service account: `python -m octg_agent connectors gsc-login --client-secret <OAuth client JSON>` signs in as your own Google user and stores a refresh token.
google_search_console.how: a Google service-account key (add its e-mail as a user of each property in Search Console) or an OAuth token from `python -m octg_agent connectors gsc-login`

bing_webmaster_tools.name: Bing Webmaster Tools
steps: In Bing Webmaster Tools (signed in as the account that has this site verified): Settings -> API access -> generate an API key.
Save the key as {folder}\bing_webmaster_api_key.txt (the file contains only the key).
bing_webmaster_tools.how: an API key generated in Bing Webmaster Tools (Settings -> API access)

map_step: In the Knowledge Hub: AI & Approvals -> Data sources -> {label} -> Map a property -> choose this client and its property, type your PIN. (Or ask the collaborator to run connectors.suggest_mapping to see which property matches the client's domain.)
